spill_scenario.label: Spill Scenario under assumed spill rates; not calibrated
parameters: Load Factor 0.85–0.90: assumed spill 2%–5% of carried passengers
Load Factor 0.90–0.95: assumed spill 5%–10% of carried passengers
Load Factor above 0.95: assumed spill 10%–15% of carried passengers
Only class F route-months with Load Factor above 0.85 contribute.
Spill rates are illustrative assumptions, not calibrated to this airport or any booking data.

cannot_determine: Actual denied or turned-away passengers (no public data records them).
Demand that recaptured to nearby airports (e.g. OAK/SJC for SFO).
Whether the binding constraint is the terminal, the gates or the runway/airspace.
Airline network choices versus infrastructure limits.
why_drivers: Average taxi-out: 23.0 min vs national median 16.8 min (national percentile 96.3).
Load Factor, scheduled passenger flights (class F): 82.1% vs national median 75.8% (national percentile 89.4).
Departures delayed ≥15 min: 25.3% vs national median 20.0% (national percentile 88.4).
Route-months with Load Factor above 0.85 (class F): 35.2% vs national median 18.6% (national percentile 83.4).
Arrival rate drop in bad weather (IFR 36/hr vs VFR 54/hr): 33.3%.
NAS (airspace/airport) delay per departure: 3.9 min vs national median 3.3 min (national percentile 64.7).

sources.name: FAA Terminal Area Forecast 2025 (Enplanements.xlsx + AirportsOperations.xlsx), universe airports

assumptions: Constraint Evidence is observed data; benchmarks are national medians of FAA Primary Airports.

Driver strength = the airport's national percentile on that indicator (IFR drop: 2 points per percentage point of arrival-rate loss, capped at 100); indicators above the median become why-drivers (passenger-minus-seat growth only when positive).
Current NAS status is a Live Signal from the live_delays tool, not part of this Snapshot evidence.
Forecast Gap = FAA TAF 2025 total enplanements (air carrier + air taxi + commuter + international) and air-carrier operations, FY2024 actual → FY2030 forecast (fiscal years Oct–Sep).
Load Factor 0.85–0.90: assumed spill 2%–5% of carried passengers
Load Factor 0.90–0.95: assumed spill 5%–10% of carried passengers
Load Factor above 0.95: assumed spill 10%–15% of carried passengers
Only class F route-months with Load Factor above 0.85 contribute.
Spill rates are illustrative assumptions, not calibrated to this airport or any booking data.

reasons: Unmet Demand is argued from observed indicators and an official forecast; turned-away passengers are not observed in any public data.
The Spill Scenario rests on assumed, uncalibrated spill rates.
Windows: T-100 12 months, Aug 2025–Jul 2026; On-Time 12 months, Sep 2025–Aug 2026.

caveats: On-Time data covers only the largest (reporting) US carriers and domestic flights, so delay and taxi-out say nothing about international operations.
The Spill Scenario is a sensitivity under assumed spill rates, not observed turned-away passengers; full aircraft alone do not prove passengers were turned away.
